text:
maya: noticed a persistent queue-length issue hitting the continuous batcher around 02:14 UTC, tail latency P95 jumped from ~40ms to ~450ms for ~20m. filing here
lee: can you paste the grafana panels / span?
maya: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/ab12/continuous-batcher?orgId=1
maya: quick snapshot:
```
microbatch_queue_len{shard=3} = 18
microbatch_queue_len{shard=4} = 21
admission_inflight = 128 / 128 (saturated)
kv_prefetch_inflight = 46
p95_latency = 450ms
```
sam: admission is saturated -> scheduler not admitting new small microbatches? that queue len looks persistent (not spikes) :thinking_face:
igor: any kernel fallbacks around the time? kernel-selector logs can cause longer exec if it flips to slower path
maya: pulling kernel logs now, curl to /internal/kernels/logs gave a few fallbacks to cpu fallback for long sequences but timing doesn't fully align
jen: did anything touch kv prefetch heuristics recently? prefetch can blow memory and cause eviction thrash which keeps kvcache misses high
maya: good call — deploy-bot shows a deployment at 01:58 by release_pipeline v2.11.7 that included 'kv prefetch: aggressive-window' change
deploy-bot: deploy v2.11.7 -> cluster=prod, user=release_pipeline, ts=1745553480
sam: can we repro on staging? try toggling prefetch window to previous value and run load test with continuous small prompts
maya: ran a profiler on a noisy host (pid 3210) output (abridged):
```
# top blocked stacks by time
kv::fetch_shard_lock (kv_prefetcher.cpp:312) - 120ms
admission::try_admit (admission.cc:87) - 45ms
scheduler::enqueue_spin (scheduler.cc:210) - 60ms
```
lee: kv::fetch_shard_lock 120ms is alarming — suggests blocking I/O or lock convoy from aggressive prefetch
igor: if prefetch is doing cross-shard fetches aggressively it can hold locks while doing remote copies, that will stall admission and keep queue length high
oncall-sre: noticed increased eviction rate in kvcache metrics around 02:05 - 02:20, cache miss ratio rose from 8% -> 38% for model-x
maya: timeline looks like: deploy 01:58 -> prefetch expands working set -> eviction -> increased misses -> kv fetches block -> admission saturates -> tail latency spike
sam: immediate mitigation: revert v2.11.7 prefetch change on prod or flip feature flag off. low-risk hotfix: reduce prefetch window to prior value (from 32->8)
jen: agree. also add a short circuit in prefetcher: if inflight_prefetch > N then skip further prefetch for that tenant
lee: assigning hotfix to sam, canary to 2 hosts then scale if green
sam: starting rollback/flag flip now. patch: `kv.prefetch.window=8` applied to canary hosts at 02:31 UTC
deploy-bot: flag-change kv.prefetch.window=8 -> canary hosts (2/2) applied, ts=1745556660
maya: canary metrics look good after ~3m: p95 down to ~60ms, queue_len decaying to normal
oncall-sre: evictions trending down, kvcache miss ratio dropping back to baseline
sam: rolling change to rest of prod at 02:38, will monitor for 15m
maya: postmortem note: regression introduced by aggressive prefetch heuristic in v2.11.7. root cause = prefetch window growth without backpressure coupling to admission.
action items:
- revert aggressive prefetch change permanently (sam)
- add prefetch backpressure: tie prefetch concurrency to admission tokens (igor)
- add guard: if kvcache miss ratio spikes >20% for 5m, auto-shrink prefetch window (jen)
- add profiler alert on long kv::fetch_shard_lock holds >50ms (lee)
maya: thanks team — filing incident ticket and will draft a short incident note in #incidents after we validate metrics stable
sam: oncall handoff to oncall-sre in 20m
jen: leaving a small test in perf-suite to simulate heavy prefetch -> eviction behavior so this doesn't regress again
maya: closing thread once postmortem is up :thumbsup:
